rationale: Both candidates independently catch the one surviving substantive ground-truth concern — the async engine's hardcoded rel_l1_thresh=0.2 default bypassing the MiniMax-H3-specific 0.17 resolution — which is strong corroborating evidence it's real. Y's writeup is materially deeper and more rigorous: it verifies the bug with an executed trace, validates the partition-separation and cross-request state claims with the same evidentiary style as the human reviewer (exact test counts, specific code paths), and surfaces additional well-grounded issues (memory retention scaling, eager RoPE computation on cached steps, E2E test that can't detect a caching regression, a drive-by frame-count change silently altering unrelated test coverage). X finds the same core bug plus some legitimate doc/CI follow-ons, but pads the list with two self-negating nits that concede they aren't real problems, weakening precision and actionability relative to Y.
